hypothesis: On printed pages where the detector is strong, host-staged geometry evidence and deterministic count verification lower character error versus the image-only baseline of the same model, keep repetition at zero, and hold invented characters within the scope-adjusted allowance on both protected scope slices.
decision: Withhold the full 28-case run and iterate the harness first. The declared smoke gates all passed (4 of 4 pairs sealed, zero repetition, budget held), so the full run was permitted, but the smoke evidence already answers the question it would have bought: toolbelt v1 wins decisively on its design case, the dense table (CER 1.349 to 0.873 with invented characters collapsing 0.380 to exactly 0.000), and loses everywhere the volume's gold excludes commentary, because the harness instructs the agent to account for every detected box (Chu Ci 0.604 to 2.000 with invented 0.595; the two ordinary pages regressed roughly twofold). This is the measured AncientDoc scope inconsistency resurfacing inside the rig. The next spend belongs to rig v2 with layered submission, not to confirming a predictable mean.

findings: The anti-hallucination property is real and large: geometry anchoring drove invented characters to exactly zero on the page where the same model invents 38 percent of its output unaided.
Repetition stayed zero on every session of both sides; the runaway class remains structurally absent under both harnesses for this model.

Box-complete transcription is the wrong target on scope_primary volumes: the count-verification loop pushes the agent to transcribe commentary the gold excludes, converting geometry fidelity into insertions.
Crop-first reading degrades ordinary pages for this model as it did for Gemini column-mode; page context remains load-bearing.
The image-only baseline is fragile on hard pages: one duplicate-submission flake in five sessions across the two runs.
